availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

value.name: wf-auto-researcher
value.description: Autonomous research subagent. Reads directions, runs experiments, benchmarks results, and commits improvements.

value.name: wf-code-reviewer
value.description: Targeted review of changed behavior and required verification. Reports blocking findings and writes the workflow verdict.

value.name: wf-coder
value.description: Reads files, edits code, runs tests, and commits. General implementation agent.

value.name: wf-design
value.description: Authors requirements and technical design documents for a feature, exploring the codebase so designs fit existing patterns.

value.name: wf-design-reviewer
value.description: Reviews technical designs for ambiguity, gaps, and unverified assumptions before implementation begins. Mechanical verdict: any HIGH/MEDIUM finding blocks.

value.name: wf-planner
value.description: Investigates a codebase and produces an ordered implementation plan — from an approved design when one is provided, or by making the design decisions itself when not.

value.name: wf-pr-responder
value.description: Responds to PR review comments and CI feedback.

value.name: wf-pr-submitter
value.description: Opens a pull request from a branch and records the PR metadata.

value.name: wf-review-aggregator
value.description: Merges multiple review outputs into a single consolidated review verdict.

value.name: wf-workflow-creator
value.description: Runs as a workflow step that designs the run's steps from a brief or an edit request, saves them with save_workflow_definition, and adds them to the run with update_workflow.

value.name: semantic_reviewer
value.description: Behavioral, narrative code review of a local or PR diff. Writes a review document and a verdict.

value.name: Explore
value.description: Analyze and understand a codebase using tree-sitter parsing and dependency graphs. Use when the user asks to analyze, explore, or generate specs for their codebase — answers structural questions about architecture, data flows, and dependencies from searches, reads and the code index, and builds architectural documentation (.kiro/specs/) with code_index_build when deep analysis is on.

value.name: create-spec
value.description: Encourages spec-driven development by producing guided artifacts — a requirements, design, and task-list specification — for a feature request.

availableCommands.name: general-task-execution
availableCommands.description: General-purpose sub-agent with access to all tools for executing arbitrary tasks

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.
